digest.component_or_area: completion-verify agent step, LLM workflow execution, runaway detection
propositions: The primary completion-verify agent step has no forced-landing boundary (tool_step_limit is never set), so budget exhaustion kills runs with no verdict instead of landing one

Three of four instrumented gate runs enter tool-call cycles (40-70% redundant calls) that the existing max_consecutive_repeat metric cannot detect, because it only counts adjacent identical calls and is blind to k-cycles with k>=2

A windowed distinct-ratio discriminator (window=24, trip<=0.50) reliably separates pathological runs (0.042-0.290) from healthy breadth (0.833+) and fires where adjacency fails, enabling a runaway actuator

The shipped forced-landing primitive (toolset filtering at tool_step_limit) breaks on Bedrock/Anthropic when tools are withdrawn mid-history, because the protocol requires toolConfig whenever history contains tool_use blocks

Synthetic tool-result steering (returning a steering notice instead of executing the repeated call) provides a protocol-safe alternative that keeps tool definitions advertised and lands a verdict through the existing finalizer without exceptions
